title.rendered: Jehovah Jireh, the Lord Will Provide: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: On the mountain where Abraham’s knife was already raised, God provided. The name Jehovah Jireh was not spoken until provision was needed most.

content.rendered:
On the mountain where Abraham’s knife was already raised, God provided. The name Jehovah Jireh was not spoken until provision was needed most.

The Gospel For Today | Wednesday, August 12, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“And Abraham called the name of the place, The-LORD-Will-Provide; as it is said to this day, ‘In the Mount of the LORD it shall be provided.’”
Genesis 22:14 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Abraham did not name God Jehovah Jireh in a season of abundance. He named Him that on Mount Moriah, knife in hand, with no ram in sight until the very last moment. The name was forged in the walk up the mountain, in three days of silence, in the moment Isaac asked where the lamb was and Abraham answered by faith alone: “God will provide Himself a lamb” (Genesis 22:8).

The Hebrew word yireh means “to see” as much as “to provide.” God’s provision is never blind improvisation — it is a God who sees the need before it fully forms and has already positioned the answer. The ram was caught in the thicket before Abraham ever climbed that mountain. It was there the whole time, waiting for the moment faith needed it revealed.

The Passion Translation captures the weight of Abraham’s declaration: “Abraham named that place ‘Yahweh-Yireh’ (which means ‘the Lord will provide’), and it has been said ever since, ‘On the mountain of the Lord, he will provide.’” (Genesis 22:14 TPT). Note the tense — not “provided,” past and finished, but “will provide,” an ongoing pattern for everyone who climbs their own mountain of testing afterward.

Every believer eventually finds themselves on some version of that mountain — a need with no visible ram, a bill with no visible income, a door with no visible key. The temptation is to panic at the empty thicket. But Jehovah Jireh’s provision has a habit of showing up exactly at the point of obedience, not before it. Abraham had to raise the knife before he saw the ram. The provision was already there; the seeing came at the moment of surrender.

If you are climbing a mountain today with your own version of an empty thicket, take courage from Abraham’s naming. God is not Jehovah Jireh only in hindsight. He is Jehovah Jireh now, at the place you have not yet reached, where the answer to your need is already caught and waiting to be seen.

Prayer

Father, You are Jehovah Jireh, the God who sees my need before I speak it and has already positioned the provision. I release the fear of the empty thicket. I trust that as I obey You one step at a time, You will show me what You have already prepared. Where I see lack, let me see instead the God who provides. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

My God is Jehovah Jireh. He sees my need before I do, and He has already provided for it. I will not panic at what looks empty. I will obey, and I will see His provision revealed at the right time.
